papers.title: Heparan sulfate sulfatases are essential for the patterning of human stem cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons.
papers.authors: Tremolanti C, Abaurre C, Chien YC, Gamon LF, Mitchell CW, Gout E, Agirre E, Lyu G, Karlsson R, Davies MJ, Castelo-Branco G, Vivès RR, Saltó C, Marklund U, Miller RL, Turnbull JE, Arenas E.
papers.abstract: Midbrain dopaminergic neurons (mDA) are selectively lost in Parkinson's disease, driving sustained efforts to generate bona fide mDA neurons from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) for replacement therapy. While morphogen gradients and transcription factors have been extensively studied, extracellular regulators remain largely overlooked. Here, we identify the heparan sulfate-modifying enzymes SULF1 and SULF2 as essential for establishing mDA neuron identity in vitro. Using CRISPR/Cas9-engineered iPSCs, we show that loss of SULF1/2 increases 6-O-sulfated heparan sulfate species and disrupts patterning both at the anteroposterior and dorsoventral axes in human iPSC-derived mDA cultures. Double-knockout cells thus fail to acquire ventral midbrain fates and instead adopt hindbrain, spinal cord and neural crest-like identities as revealed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Mechanistically, we partially explain the changed patterning to aberrant FGF signaling and demonstrate that FGF inhibition redirects cells toward midbrain fates, however without restoring ventral identity. These findings establish a critical role for SULF1/2 in mDA neuron in vitro differentiation and uncover a previously unrecognized layer of extracellular control over neural patterning.

papers.title: Retinal Structure Reflects Cumulative Blast Exposure and Blast-Related Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.authors: Gustafson JA, Walter K, Parenteau C, Hao S, Fortier CB, Milberg WP, Fortenbaugh FC.
papers.abstract: Objective U.S. military service members experienced a high rate of blast exposures during post-9/11 military conflicts. Though a growing body of literature suggests that these exposures have long term consequences for health, objective biomarkers of blast-related neurotrauma remain limited. We used optical coherence tomography (OCT) to determine whether blast-related mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) and cumulative blast exposure burden were associated with retinal microstructural changes. Design A retrospective, cross-sectional cohort study at VA Boston Healthcare System. Participants Seventy-three United States post 9/11 veterans enrolled in the Translational Research Center for TBI & Stress Disorders (TRACTS) longitudinal cohort study who underwent OCT imaging based on assessment availability. Methods Principal observations were blast-related mild traumatic brain injury and cumulative lifetime blast exposure burden. Main outcomes measures Retinal thickness as measured by high-resolution Spectralis OCT imaging, including 7 individual macular layers, combined macular layers (inner retina, outer retina, and total retina), and the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer, using automated segmentation software. Results Among 73 participants (mean [SD] age, 40.8 [9.4] years; 63 [86%] male), 25 had a history of blast mTBI (blast mTBI+) and 48 did not (blast mTBI-). Participants with blast mTBI+ had significantly thicker retinal layers in the macula, specifically in the 3mm quadrants around the fovea. The peripapillary RNFL (pRNFL) was significantly thinner in the blast mTBI+ group (p = .009), with the most significant thinning occurring nasally, most notably superior/nasal (p Conclusions Retinal structural measures distinguished veterans with blast-related mild traumatic brain injury and predicted cumulative blast exposure burden. These findings support OCT as an accessible approach for identifying retinal biomarkers of blast-related neurotrauma and cumulative blast exposure.

papers.title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma.
papers.authors: Arnould M, Assie JB, Meiller C, Sequeiros R, Imbeaud S, Roehrig A, Boano C, Le Corre D, Mouillet-Richard S, Poupel L, Lavergne J, Hofman V, Hofman P, Humez S, Scherpereel A, Le Pimpec-Barthes F, Zucman-Rossi J, Blanquart C, Jaurand MC, Lantuejoul S, Hirsch TZ, Damotte D, Jean D.
papers.abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

papers.title: Immune infiltrate predicts response to αPD1/αCTLA4 but not αPD1 and distinguishes programs of primary resistance in metastatic melanoma.
papers.authors: Huang AY, Burke KP, Glettig MC, Porter R, Fatouros P, Li JM, Meiger L, Rosado V, Xu S, Yang J, Robitschek E, Vokes N, Ricker C, Tarantino G, Chen J, Aprati TJ, He Y, Wang C, Fu D, Ho LL, Galani K, Freeman GJ, Buchbinder EI, Hodi FS, Lian CG, Kellis M, Boland GM, Sharpe AH, Liu D.
papers.abstract: While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti-PD-1 ( n = 290), anti-CTLA-4 ( n = 175), and combination anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4 ( n = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4 compared to anti-PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti-PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti-PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

papers.title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations.
papers.authors: Bischoff S, Poličar PG, Mukherjee S, Macke JH, Claassen M, Schröder C.
papers.abstract: Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

papers.title: Association of allergic conjunctivitis severity with meibomian gland abnormalities in children: a cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Yan J, Du J, Deng Y, Chen Y, Chen W, Li J.
papers.abstract: Purpose To evaluate associations of allergic conjunctivitis (AC) severity with meibomian gland structure and function and tear film stability in children. Design Single-center, cross-sectional study. Participants The primary analysis included 144 children: 32 healthy controls and 112 patients with active AC classified as mild (n = 42), moderate (n = 39), or severe (n = 31). Supplementary analyses included 141 adults. Methods Participants underwent standardized ocular surface examinations and noncontact meibography. AC severity was classified according to ocular surface signs. Multivariable linear regression evaluated severity-related associations after adjustment for age, sex, and disease duration. Main outcome measures Total meibomian gland loss (MGL), fluorescein breakup time (FBUT), gland morphology scores, and meibum quality and expressibility scores. Results Median total MGL was 9.00%, 20.50%, 31.00%, and 36.00% in the control, mild, moderate, and severe groups, respectively. Corresponding median FBUT values were 9.50, 4.00, 3.00, and 2.00 seconds (both overall P Conclusions Greater AC severity was associated with greater MGL and reduced tear film stability in children. Meibum quality grade, however, did not differ significantly across groups. These findings support including meibomian gland and tear film assessments in the clinical evaluation of pediatric AC. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between AC severity and gland abnormalities.

papers.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke's area.
papers.authors: Silva AB, Leonard MK, Hullett PW, Levy DF, Wang C, Xu D, Bhaya-Grossman I, Chang EF.
papers.abstract: Wernicke's area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke's area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke's area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

papers.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme.
papers.authors: El Nesr G, Dürr SL, Mathews II, Wen Q, Zhao K, Sarangi R, Rothlisberger U, Sunden F, Huang PS.
papers.abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

papers.title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces.
papers.authors: Wang S, Li R, Tang Z, Li Y, Gong C, Song WJ, Lim CT, Chen X, Zhao X.
papers.abstract: Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase-free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue-like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.

papers.title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation.
papers.authors: Rambout X, Nagao R, Gu V, Werner S, Youngyunpipatkul J, Schlierf J, Pröschel C, Maquat LE.
papers.abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron-containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

papers.title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis.
papers.authors: Boesger HA, Fang E, Wang R, Harte RJ, Koroleva A, Tunckanat T, Momin AN, Elliott SJ, Metsä-Ketelä M, Newmister SA, Sherman DH.
papers.abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

papers.title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress.
papers.authors: Borruto AM, Kohlund T, Rettig L, von Renesse M, Hammer CA, Leonhardt N, Kurpiers B, Calpe-López C, Benn L, Friederich HC, Kuner T, Spanagel R, Wieland S.
papers.abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to-central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

papers.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans.
papers.authors: Yu X, Li Y, Shi G, Yu L, Wang Y, Lai S, Zhou Y, Zhang Y, Sun N, Zhang B, Hu Y, Li Z, Jiang Y, Li W, Fu TM, Yu JZ.
papers.abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year -1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year -1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year -1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

papers.title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells.
papers.authors: Li B, Zhang T, Wang X, Wen Y, Wang Y, Yu X, Yang D.
papers.abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

papers.title: Quaternary carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles.
papers.authors: Hu XD, Zheng YQ, Zhai K, Li TY, Guo ZX, Li JL, Liu WB.
papers.abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

papers.title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling.
papers.authors: Lee S, Weingarten EA, Reynolds MF, Sun K, Cortese AJ, Davies HML, Molnar AC, McEuen PL, Lin S.
papers.abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.

papers.title: Space-map: 3D single-cell atlas reconstruction from serial sections.
papers.authors: Han R, Ruan C, Zhao B, Tan Y, Monte E, Wei B, Bi J, Karathanos TV, Laquindanum R, Charville GW, Lin Y, Ling N, Ford JM, Nolan GP, Wang M, Zhu C, Snyder MP.
papers.abstract: High-resolution three-dimensional (3D) tissue atlases promise to link cellular architecture to tissue function, but assembling them from serial sections containing millions of cells remains challenging. Here we present Space-map, an accurate and efficient method for reconstructing 3D tissue models from high-content spatial molecular profiles. Space-map combines multiscale feature matching with large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping to automate global alignment across serial sections while preserving local microanatomy. We generate spatial transcriptomics (Xenium; ~2.7 million cells) and proteomics (CODEX; ~4.8 million cells) datasets from serial sections to build 3D models of a colon polyp and healthy intestinal tissues. These models reveal cell-type heterogeneity in the polyp and preserved crypt and glandular architecture and mucosal-cavity continuity in healthy intestines. Benchmarking on our own and publicly available datasets demonstrates that Space-map achieves substantially higher registration accuracy and up to a tenfold speedup over existing methods, supporting its use as a robust framework for constructing 3D human tissue atlases at single-cell resolution.

papers.title: Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination.
papers.authors: Struijs JJC, Crumpton AE, Gouverneur V, Aldridge S.
papers.abstract: New catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement 1 , particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca-F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F - capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F - shuttling. Late Ca-F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F - by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

papers.title: Low-Concentration Atropine Eye Drops in Children With Myopia and Intermittent Exotropia: The AMIXT2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Zuo X, Tang H, Zhang Y, Li T, Xie Y, Leng Z, Chen X, Wang L, Wang X, Liu H.
papers.abstract: Importance The optimal atropine concentration for myopia control in children with coexisting intermittent exotropia (IXT) remains uncertain. Objective To compare the efficacy and safety of 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine eye drops in children with myopia and IXT. Design, setting, and participants This single-center, double-masked, 3-arm randomized clinical trial was conducted from September 2023 to March 2026. Children aged 6 to 12 years with basic-type IXT and myopia (cycloplegic spherical equivalent [SE], -0.50 to -6.00 diopters [D]) were enrolled. Data analysis was conducted from March 2026 to July 2026. Interventions Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to 0.01%, 0.02%, or 0.04% atropine eye drops nightly in both eyes. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcome was 12-month change in cycloplegic SE. Secondary outcomes included changes in axial length (AL), exotropia conditions, binocular vision, and ocular safety parameters. Results Among 264 randomized children (mean [SD] age, 8.4 [1.5] years; 130 female [49.2%]), 224 (84.8%) completed the 12-month assessment. Mean (SD) SE changes were -0.43 (0.50) D, -0.35 (0.51) D, and -0.18 (0.60) D with 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine, respectively (overall P = .001). Compared with 0.01% and 0.02% atropine, 0.04% atropine was associated with less SE progression (vs 0.01%: difference, 0.24 D; 95% CI, 0.11-0.37 D; P Conclusions and relevance In the AMIXT2 randomized clinical trial among children with myopia and IXT, 0.04% atropine eye drops were associated with less myopia progression and axial elongation over 12 months than 0.01% or 0.02% atropine eye drops. Higher concentrations were associated with greater reductions in near magnitude of exodeviation, which warrant further investigation. Trial registration chictr.org.cn Identifier: ChiCTR2300075312.
